title: Acceptance framework for cost-driven batching with waterfall sentinels
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an automated acceptance framework that evaluates and gates batch/cache configuration recommendations produced by the cost optimizer. Instead of a single pass/fail gate we will implement a deterministic, staged 'waterfall sentinels' approach that progressively relaxes cost constraints while tracking multidimensional quality signals. The goal is to enable safe automated apply and fast rollback of cost-driven changes with strong statistical guarantees and clear operator visibility.
goals: Reduce per-token serving cost by automating safe application of batching/cache profiles
Prevent customer-facing quality regressions via multi-stage acceptance checks
Provide reproducible, auditable evaluation artifacts (golden prompts, ranked metrics, diffs) for every automated change
Enable fast automated rollback and human-in-the-loop review for borderline cases
success_criteria: Automated applies achieve >= 8% median token-cost reduction on canary traffic without exceeding quality regressions thresholds
False-positive rollback rate < 5% over a 30-day rolling window
End-to-end apply-to-observation latency < 20 minutes for standard canaries
All applied changes have associated evaluation artifacts stored and linked in the run log
technical_solution: Cost optimizer outputs candidate batch/cache profile with expected cost delta and simulated latency distribution
Evaluation runner executes a layered test plan: unit synthetic checks -> golden prompt suite -> production shadow canary -> lightweight online A/B for 1% traffic

Waterfall sentinels: a sequence of progressively permissive gates (strict local offline, expanded offline with augmentations, shadow apply, micro-canary, full canary) each with independent metrics and thresholds

Aggregated quality score computed as weighted combination of semantic similarity (ROUGE/embedding similarity), behavioral checks (hallucination proxies, response length drift), and business signals (error rate, latency deviations)
Automated decision engine applies candidate when aggregate score passes at a specified sentinel level; otherwise triggers manual review or immediate rollback rules
Every apply is stored with immutable evaluation artifacts (inputs, references, outputs, metric traces) for audit and reproduction
evaluation_suite: Golden prompt bank (500 prompts) stratified by domain, length, and temperature sensitivity
Reference answer corpus for deterministic prompts where available; model agnostic similarity baselines for open prompts
Behavioral checks: instruction-following probes, refusal tests, entity hallucination probes
Statistical tests: paired bootstrap for median token-level metrics, permutation test for embedding similarity, control chart drift detection for latency and error rate
Shadow-run harness to replay recent production requests through candidate config without affecting real responses
golden_prompts_sample: Prompt: 'Summarize the following user support ticket in two sentences and list possible next actions.' — verifies instruction condensation and action extraction
Prompt: 'Explain the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption in simple terms.' — verifies factual integrity and brevity
Prompt: 'Given product release notes, produce three TL;DR bullets for executives.' — checks summarization and key-finding
Prompt: 'Refuse instructions that request personal data disclosure and show a policy-safe reply.' — verifies guardrails and refusal behavior
acceptance_thresholds: Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) delta: must not drop more than 0.015 median compared to baseline on golden set
ROUGE-L median change: > -0.03 tolerated for cost-first candidates, stricter -0.01 for high-risk customers
Behavioral failure rate: absolute increase < 0.2% and relative increase < 10%
Latency p95: must not increase by more than 15ms on canary traffic
Error rate (500s/timeout): absolute increase < 0.05% within first 24h
Cost reduction: candidate must show >= 3% estimated token cost improvement at minimum to be considered for apply
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Offline unit checks (sanity, config validation) — immediate pass/fail
Stage 1: Golden-set offline run — require thresholds pass
Stage 2: Shadow apply for 1 hour on sampled 0.1% traffic — collect response diffs and latency traces
Stage 3: Micro-canary: route 0.5% traffic for 2 hours with automated scoring and human review window
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 5% and 20% with monitoring checks; at each step recompute aggregated quality score
Stage 5: Full rollout policy execution or automated rollback if sentinel fires
rollback_policy: Immediate automatic rollback triggers: behavioral failure spike > threshold, latency degradation beyond p95 threshold, or runtime errors above baseline
Soft rollback: pause ramp and notify on-call for manual inspection if minor metric deviations observed
Post-rollback analysis: capture last-known-good artifacts, candidate artifacts, diff report, and schedule blameless postmortem if customer impact was high
Transparency: notify downstream customers and record decision in audit log with link to evaluation artifacts
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard tile: candidate vs baseline cost delta, embedding similarity, ROUGE, behavioral fail rate, latency p50/p95
Alert: sentinel_fire (critical) when automated rollback executed
Alert: quality_degradation_warning (warning) when offline golden set drifts but not yet failing production
Daily digest: applied_changes with aggregated metrics and link to artifacts
SLOs: ensure < 0.5% of paid customers see >TTR increase due to apply within 72h
test_matrix_and_runs: Unit tests for config parser and simulator (run on PR)
Offline regression runs against nightly golden bank (scheduled) — baseline vs candidate comparisons
Canary runs on synthetic traffic (CI) and 0.5% production micro-canary
Chaos tests: introduce induced latency and error injections to validate rollback reactions
A/B live test for correlated business metrics for top 5 customers (manual opt-in)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Golden prompts may not cover emergent user patterns — Mitigation: continuous addition pipeline and periodic sampling from production
Risk: False negatives from embedding drift — Mitigation: multi-metric aggregation and threshold tuning via historical analysis
Risk: Automated rollback flapping — Mitigation: cooldown windows and rate-limited automated rollback actions
Risk: Operator overload from noisy alerts — Mitigation: implement priority scoring and root-cause clustering for related sentinels
notes: This approach favors auditable reproducibility over black-box heuristics; every decision must have stored artifacts for review.
We will prioritize integration with Console run logs and existing rollouts pipeline to reuse canary routing primitives.
Consider a future extension to let customers opt into 'aggressive cost saver' tier with relaxed thresholds.
